title: the-watcher-asks-a-row-that-exists
intention: The codebase watcher's escalation to inference names a domain row and a model the live inference_domain serves, takes the answer's text as its finding, and records a refusal as an escalation error instead of a finding of nothing.
why: Akien 2026-10-05 (/home/akien/.cairn/foreground-decisions.md 8h): 'every requester that gets something they can't do should throw a ticket'. The lived symptom: codemother's watcher has never had an escalation answered — 689 of 689 refused replies in ~/.cairn/devices/codemother/0/mail say "no domain row named 'codemother' in the domains stack" — and each refusal was recorded as a finding of nothing, so the watcher looked like it was working.
traces_to: Law 7 (errors are loud at diagnostic surfaces: a refusal wrapped as an empty finding is the collapse a record may never make); Akien 8h 2026-10-05 (an unfillable request is a trouble — here the requester side stops swallowing the refusal); RULE 1 (the watcher asks inference_domain only through its bus verb, and the fix lives in codemother); codemother's charter (the watcher face reasons through inference_proxy, not Claude)
how: In cairn/devices/codemother/watch.py _escalate_to_hex, send domain 'coding' (a row in inference_domain's domains stack, preferring qwen3-coder:30b) and model 'qwen3-coder:30b' instead of domain 'codemother' and model 'qwen'; read a reply whose outcome is 'refused' as {nodes: [], error}; take answer['text'] as the node content. In activate(), record escalation_error when the escalation returns an error, not only when it raises. Proof cairn/devices/codemother/proofs/test_the_watcher_asks_a_row_that_exists.py, written red 0/4.
falsifier: GREEN when cairn/devices/codemother/proofs/test_the_watcher_asks_a_row_that_exists.py prints four ok lines and exits 0 with the live bus and inference host up: (1) _escalate_to_hex over the live bus returns no error and a node of non-empty text; (2) a reply with outcome 'refused' yields no nodes and an error naming its detail; (3) an answer {text: T} yields a node whose content is T; (4) activate records escalation_error when the escalation returns an error; and `python3 -m pytest -q cairn/devices/codemother/proofs/test_watch.py` passes. RED if any fails. Wrong intent if the watcher should have its own domain row in inference_domain instead of riding 'coding'.
watchme: none, because (cairn/devices/codemother/watch.py _log_activation) every activation already writes its record under ~/.cairn/devices/codemother/0/watch/activations, and after this ticket a refused escalation lands there as escalation_error, so the refusal rate is countable from records that already exist with no probe
children: none, because the change is one function pair (_escalate_to_hex, activate) in one file of one component with one proof on disk

decisions.text: D1: SETTLED: apply exactly the unified diff carried in this ticket's build_patch field (`git apply` from a file holding that text, run in the cairn repo root). It edits only cairn/devices/codemother/watch.py: _escalate_to_hex sends domain 'coding' and model 'qwen3-coder:30b'; a reply body with outcome 'refused' returns {nodes: [], error: 'refused (<refused>): <detail>'}; otherwise the node content is answer['text'] when the answer is a dict; activate() sets record['escalation_error'] when the escalation returns an error. No other code changes.

D2: SETTLED: the proof cairn/devices/codemother/proofs/test_the_watcher_asks_a_row_that_exists.py is already on disk, committed red at d756cbd3 (0 of 4 at HEAD). After the build it prints four ok lines and exits 0 (tooth 1 needs the live bus and the inference host); the regression `python3 -m pytest -q cairn/devices/codemother/proofs/test_watch.py` passes.

D3: SETTLED: tooth 1 of the proof asks the LIVE inference_domain over the LIVE bus — that is the falsifier (test against live, ruled 2026-09-28), not a setup step. The builder starts nothing: the bus and inference_domain are already running on this box (the system lazy-inits on any cairn command, I-the-command-lazy-inits-the-system.md). If tooth 1 reds with a timeout or connection error rather than a refusal, the build is not wrong — report the error verbatim and stop; teeth 2-4 use fake buses and need nothing running.
